content: Interventions aimed at inducing mucosal healing in patients with ulcerative colitis focus on achieving complete resolution of inflammation in the colonic mucosa. Mucosal healing is considered a critical therapeutic goal, as it is associated with improved long-term outcomes, including reduced risk of disease relapse, hospitalization, and colorectal cancer. Various pharmacological treatments are utilized to achieve this objective, including aminosalicylates, corticosteroids, immunomodulators, and biologic agents such as anti-TNF therapies, anti-integrin agents, and IL-12/23 inhibitors. The choice of therapy depends on the severity of the disease, patient-specific factors, and prior treatment responses.
